title: Lamb or Mutton with Noodles in Gravy

content.title: About
content.content: Lamb (or mutton) with noodles in a rich gravy is a classic dish that pairs tender meat with hearty noodles coated in a thick, flavorful sauce. The meat is slow‑cooked until juicy, while the gravy often includes tomatoes, spices and sometimes cream, giving the dish a deep, savory taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lamb is a good source of iron and zinc, making it a valuable micronutrient provider.
The dish has roots in Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisines, where noodles are sometimes replaced with homemade pasta or vermicelli.
Combining meat and noodles in gravy is popular in Asian street food, where quick stir‑frying is used.
Mutton is considered richer and more aromatic than adult lamb due to its higher fat content.
In some regions, yogurt or kefir is added to the gravy to mellow the spice heat.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Lamb provides all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: High in iron
items.content: The iron in lamb is highly bioavailable and helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is crucial for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and promotes wound healing.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of meat and noodles offers lasting satiety and fuel for active days.

items.title: High in saturated fat
items.content: Lamb contains saturated fats, so people with cardiovascular concerns should watch portion size.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to lamb.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Lamb is relatively high in cholesterol; those with hypercholesterolemia should consume it moderately.

items.title: Salt in the gravy
items.content: Gravies often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, often garnished with fresh herbs (parsley, cilantro) and lemon wedges. You can add vegetables such as tomatoes or bell peppers, or a dollop of yogurt sauce for freshness. Toss the noodles in the gravy so they fully absorb the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a splash of water or broth to prevent the gravy from becoming too thick.
